overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing a citizen's petition not listed on the September 26 notice; the crowd-access, post-adjournment deliberation, and item-order complaints were not violations or were declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board denied access to the September 26 meeting by telling attendees to leave the room before it began.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board made reasonable accommodations for the anticipated crowd and was prepared to continue the meeting rather than deny access to those who wished to attend, we find no violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board discussed a citizen's petition at the September 26 meeting although it was not listed on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law when it discussed the petition to remove the Town Administrator without listing that topic on the notice of the September 26 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant objected that the petition was discussed at the very end of the meeting, when some attendees had already stopped watching.
allegations.key_passage: Nothing within the Open Meeting Law dictates the order of items to be discussed at a meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged two members continued deliberating after the September 26 meeting adjourned while remaining in the room.
allegations.key_passage: As there is no evidence that members of the Board deliberated outside of a meeting, we find no violation on this point.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, with a caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
